propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape does not enforce the overstated headline guarantee ('A child never runs ahead of its parent'); §I4a must be narrowed to what the table actually guarantees: per-edge, same-edge cascades paired with a store invariant (no non-terminal child under closed ancestor) jointly maintained by the table's closed-source rows and the unconditional close guard.

Reactivating a closed child to in_progress under an open parent does not cascade (only a closed parent is eligible on that edge); this residual is accepted and documented as intended, pinned by test_reactivate_does_not_disturb_open_parent.

The blocked -> in_progress transition does not cascade even though the start-work gate fires on it; this is resolved as documented non-cascading because: (a) a blocked child cannot sit under a closed ancestor (the unconditional close guard prevents it), (b) the table's same-edge shape means only a blocked parent could be eligible, and auto-resuming an independently-blocked parent is wrong, (c) the gate and cascade answer different questions and are consistent when documented together.

The operator-ruled invariant is required: no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket; this is enforced jointly by the cascade table and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py.
No transition refused today becomes permitted and the claim-status guard (txn.claim_core) remains untouched; the _CASCADING_EDGES table rows are byte-for-byte unchanged.
